title: What exact execution failure appears?
summary: Permission, command lookup, interpreter, format, and environment failures need different checks.

choices.label: No such file or directory / bad interpreter
Works interactively but not in cron/Jenkins/systemd

title: Which permission boundary blocks execution?
summary: Check execute bits, directory traversal, user identity, ACLs, mount options, and security controls without broadening permissions.

commands.purpose: Inspect each parent-directory permission where available.
Identify the backing mount and options.

title: Can the intended shell resolve the command?
summary: Interactive aliases, functions, virtual environments, and PATH entries may not exist in automation contexts.

commands.purpose: Show how the current shell resolves the command.
Locate the command without executing it.

choices.label: Command is not installed or path is wrong

title: Does the shebang name a real interpreter without CRLF corruption?
summary: A visible script can fail with “No such file” when its interpreter or loader is missing.

commands.purpose: Inspect file type and line-ending clues.

title: Does the executable match the host architecture and format?
summary: Wrong architecture, missing dynamic loader, or attempting to execute data can produce format/loader failures.

title: What differs in the real automation environment?
summary: User, PATH, shell, working directory, environment variables, mounts, and permissions can differ from an interactive terminal.

title: Apply the minimum required execute/traverse permission
summary: Grant only the intended user/group permission; never use chmod 777 as a generic fix.
prerequisites: Current mode and parent permissions recorded
rollback: Restore the previous mode/ACL if access becomes too broad or behavior changes.
verification: Intended user can execute while unrelated users do not gain unnecessary access.

title: Respect the noexec boundary
summary: Move the executable to an approved executable filesystem or use the intended interpreter only if policy permits; do not remount broadly by default.

title: Inspect the denial evidence
summary: Review ACL, SELinux, AppArmor, or sandbox logs and correct the smallest wrong policy/configuration; do not disable controls.

title: Install or reference the intended command through the approved mechanism
summary: Confirm package/source and environment before changing the host.

choices.label: Software source or version is unclear

rollback: Remove the new package/path change and restore the previous environment configuration.
verification: Correct command resolves for the intended user and context.

title: Set a narrow explicit PATH or absolute command path
summary: Avoid global PATH changes when only one script/service needs the command.
rollback: Restore the prior environment or command path.
verification: The intended binary resolves in the real execution context.

title: Correct the intended interpreter path
summary: Use an installed, supported interpreter and preserve script semantics.
verification: Script executes with the intended interpreter and behavior.

title: Convert only the affected script to expected line endings
summary: Preserve content and repository policy while removing CRLF from the shebang/script.
rollback: Restore the previous file from version control.
verification: Shebang resolves and script behavior remains correct.

title: Use a binary built for the target platform
summary: Replace only after verifying architecture, loader, source, and integrity.

choices.label: Supply chain or platform is unclear

verification: Binary loads and executes in the target environment.

title: Make the automation context explicit
summary: Set only required environment, working directory, shell, and paths; do not copy an entire interactive environment or embed secrets.
prerequisites: Real execution user and environment identified
rollback: Restore the previous service/job/script configuration and remove temporary debug output.
verification: Execution succeeds in the real cron/Jenkins/systemd context.

title: Verify least-privilege execution in the real context
summary: Interactive success alone is insufficient when automation originally failed.
verification: Intended user resolves and executes the intended command

title: Escalate with exact error and execution context
summary: Record user, shell, command path, file type, mount options, and sanitized environment differences.

title: Diagnosis complete
summary: The reviewed recovery checks passed. Record the cause and prevention step before closing the incident.
prevention: Document the confirmed cause and exact recovery.
Add monitoring or a regression check where practical.
